summary: Retest of 4 acceptance criteria (module hub/runner/result view transitions not using stale memoized UI, recorder/device cleanup safety, frontend type-safety after hook changes, mock title-accurate interactions) via the backend pytest suite (4 files, all passing, unchanged) + a real composite `tsc -b` type-check + re-running 13 existing browser checks by name. Two checks failed on first run and were root-caused to stale TEST ARTIFACTS, not app bugs: (1) listening-audio-stops-on-page-change assumed every Listening question used the button-triggered synth player (data-testid play-listening-audio-button); the module test this run landed on the native <audio controls> variant (listening-audio-progress-player) instead, so the old assertions (pause()/cancel() call counts) never applied - fixed to detect both player variants and, for the native-audio variant, assert playback actually stops by checking the element is detached from the DOM and no longer playing after navigating away. (2) mock-timing-has-start-pause-controls asserted a 'mock-paused-notice' banner that the ACTIVE MockRunner component (pages/Home.tsx, the one actually rendered for view==='mock') never implements - only an older, unused MockRunnerLegacy variant has that banner. Fixed the check to assert the pause state that this component actually guarantees: the countdown timer freezes and the Next/Finish button becomes disabled while paused. After these fixes, both checks and the full remaining suite pass. One unrelated timeout on this same check's first attempt was traced to a single slow mock-generation call (~40s, confirmed healthy via direct backend curl) and passed cleanly on immediate re-run - classified flaky, not a bug. Removed stray .backup scratch files from the checks directory per fixture-discipline rules.
